Start by moving the device up to three finger widths above your wrist bone, then experiment with slightly lower placement. Installation Instructions:  1: Flip the Tow/Run Switch to the TOW position (this should be done whenever you are servicing the cart)  2: Disconnect main positive and negative battery cables to your cart 3: Remove the ADC speed sensor from the end of your cart motor  4: Now you can gain access to the magnet. Simple remove the magnet by using a small flat head screwdriver or socket  5: Install the new magnet in the same position you just remove the old magnet from 6: No just re-install the speed sensor, re-attach the battery cables, and run the Tow/Run switch back to the RUN position. If your model number starts with "1510" then you also have an IQ system.  This magnet will fit, but will NOT work on vehicles equipped with the Excel system. Excel vehicles have serial number prefixes of PH, PJ, PU or PD This magnet is a "half-pulse" magnet. Once installed on your motor it will still communicate to the speed sensor exactly as the other magnet did, but only half as often. This magnet won't give you a boost of power or torque it merely raises the electronic rev limiter so high that the vehicle will never reach it. In turn, you will be able to run the full potential of your vehicle..The regenerative motor braking becomes completely disabled when this magnet is installed and will allow you to "free-wheel" down hills. The magnet in this listing will fit any Club Car vehicle with the IQ drive system that is equipped with an ADC motor. There were two motors available with the IQ system. 1. GE - The GE is grey in color and uses a snap-in speed sensor. 2. ADC - The ADC motor uses a speed sensor shaped like a top hat that bolts on.
